$comment: A SECOND NAME OF A DEFINITION ON MACH-O (P69, lane cs): the GNU `alias("target")` attribute is REFUSED BY NAME there. MEASURED (lane cs, probe-reference-cc): Apple clang refuses every alias it was given ('aliases are not supported on darwin'), while gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 build and run the same declarations on ELF and PE (examples/c/symbol_alias_second_name). Each Mach-O document states why (`symbolAliasUnsupportedReason`: the platform's own compilers refuse one), and the semantic tier reads that statement, so the refusal is the document's and names nothing in code. Before the alias was built the clause was dropped with a warning and the name stayed a reference nobody defines. NO `runOn`: the refusal is a cross-compile fact observable from any host.
